item.title: About
item.author: jparedescolmenarejo@gmail.com (Jose Paredes)
item.description:
I am a computer vision and ML engineer based in Madrid. At EIPSA I build computer vision systems and data automation for industrial engineering, from inspection models on the production line to the tooling that surrounds them. Outside of work I build local-first AI products: tools that run on your own machine and keep your data there.

Resume: PDF

Languages: Spanish (native) · English (B2)

Projects

  • Subany — live subtitles in the browser. Whisper and ONNX on WebGPU, with no server round-trip.
  • subany.site — the project site for subany.video.
  • CleanYourMail — a local-first way to clean up a Gmail inbox without handing over your mail.
  • CleanYourPhone — the same idea for your phone: inspect and clean it locally.
  • DocFlow — document automation for industrial teams.
  • Pro POV CS2 — a computer-vision project for Counter-Strike 2 POV clips.
  • GitHub — the rest of the code, including the models published on Hugging Face.

Computer Vision / Object Detection

Object detection models

A curated model zoo of 14 YOLO-based detectors for industrial inspection, esports and real-time computer vision. Weights, metrics and training notebooks, with models published on Hugging Face.

item.description:
This site is a personal portfolio run by Jose Paredes, based in Madrid, Spain. It has no accounts, no comments and no newsletter, and no data is sold. This page explains what is collected when you visit, why, and how to opt out.

Google Analytics (only with your consent)

The site uses Google Analytics 4 (measurement ID G-Y85VJ3E6W4) to understand how the site is used: which pages are read, how visitors arrive and which content is useful. The legal basis is your consent: the analytics script loads only after you accept the cookie banner. If you decline, it never loads.

item.title: Projects
item.author: jparedescolmenarejo@gmail.com (Jose Paredes)
item.description:
Three builds, each with the problem, what I did and the result. Everything here is live or in production.

Case studies

Industrial computer vision

Problem. Penetrant and weld inspection depends on a trained eye: defects are small, varied and easy to miss at production pace.

What I did. Trained YOLO11 detectors for fluorescent penetrant indications and welding defects, and published 10+ models on Hugging Face.

Result. In production — the detectors run on real inspection work, not a benchmark.

  • YOLO11
  • Hugging Face

Penetrant model on Hugging Face · More models · Welding detector on GitHub

DocFlow — document control SaaS

Problem. Engineering project orders generate documents that must be tracked, reviewed and signed across email and the ERP.

What I did. Built the internal SaaS end to end: a FastAPI backend with 21 API routers and 24 services, a React frontend with 24 screens, DocuSign for signatures, JWT auth, and Docker + CI for deployment.

Result. In production and in daily use.

  • FastAPI
  • React
  • DocuSign
  • JWT
  • Docker
  • CI

The public repository is DocFlow Lite, a CustomTkinter desktop app; the SaaS described here is internal.

DocFlow Lite on GitHub

subany.video — subtitles in the browser

Problem. Live streams have no subtitles in the viewer’s language, and server-side transcription adds cost and latency.

What I did. Built a fixed-delay player with Whisper speech recognition, Silero VAD and ONNX/WebGPU inference — all in the browser, no servers.

Result. Measured 15.3 s fixed delay against a 15 s target, with a median subtitle offset of 0–40 ms.

  • Whisper
  • Silero VAD
  • ONNX/WebGPU
